newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican bond trading on bolsa sees slow start.
newsitem.headline: Mexican bond trading on bolsa sees slow start.

text.p: The first day of trading for Mexican sovereign long-term bonds on the Mexican stock exchange started slowly on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said much of the reason for the low volume was due to a reluctance on the part of many market players to buy the paper before the rules under which they would trade became clearer.
"There were five operations at the end, but they were not significant," said one analyst.
The total volume was only 360,000 issues traded.
The first debt instruments listed were Mexican government bonds, or United Mexican States (UMS), and Brady bonds.

The Finance Ministry said earlier the move to list the bonds was aimed at opening direct access for local investors to public debt, increasing their investment opportunities and creating a long-term debt market in Mexico.
The dollar-denominated instruments will be settled in pesos.

The instruments were seen traded by brokerage houses and banks and the government believes the buyers will be financial institutions, public investors, institutional investors, investment funds and the new private pension funds.
